acceptance_excerpt: This paper studies an auditable public-data-oriented U.S. equity research workflow linking security screening, SEC-derived characteristics, internally constructed factor portfolios, asset-pricing models, constrained allocations, and walk-forward prediction. The frozen sample screens 822 securities, accepts 487, and contains 715,447 market observations and 37,273 fundamental observations. Of 48 configured factor names, 47 have nonmissing raw values; these are neither independent signals nor uniformly available observations. Corrected holding endpoints produce 11,352 quantile-portfolio observations. On matched per-asset samples, mean adjusted R-squared ranges from 0.760818 for CAPM to 0.817658 for FF5, with negative mean cycle intercepts and no intercept surviving supplementary Holm adjustment across 615 tests. Eight long-only allocation methods are evaluated over 31 complete monthly trading cycles. CVaR has the highest observed cumulative net return, 73.68%, but descriptive rankings do not establish durable superiority. The corrected two-characteristic ML panel has 27,632 rows, 89 common monthly dates, and 15 dependent test folds. Exploratory mean-IC intervals are nominally positive for the linear families, cross zero for random forest, and are negative for XGBoost. Stable incremental after-cost economic value has not been established: the implemented economic check holds selected equities for one subsequent session, not a continuous 21-session strategy. The contribution is integrated, traceable empirical evaluation with explicit source-vintage, timing, dependence, and implementation limits.
